summary: Describes an architecture for Pseudo Wire Emulation Edge-to-Edge (PWE3), emulating services such as Frame Relay, ATM, Ethernet, TDM, and SONET/SDH over packet networks using IP or MPLS, and presents the framework for pseudo wires.

eli5.summary: It makes an old-style cable seem to exist across a modern shared network, so the two ends behave as though joined by a dedicated wire.

questions: how does a pseudo wire work over mpls
subtitle: The architecture for emulating wires such as T1, Frame Relay, ATM and Ethernet across IP and MPLS networks.

tldr.problem: Carriers and customers had services such as Frame Relay, ATM, Ethernet, TDM and SONET/SDH that behave like dedicated wires, and wanted to carry them over a shared packet switched network instead.
tldr.mechanism: A pseudo wire between two provider edge devices encapsulates the native bits, cells or packets, adds sequencing and timing when needed, and sends them through a tunnel across an IP or MPLS network. A layered model separates the payload, the demultiplexer and the network.
tldr.outcome: The RFC gives the terminology, reference models and layering that later PWE3 documents build on, and leaves wire formats and signaling protocols to them. It is updated by RFC 5462.

facts.label: Payload types
facts.value: 4 (packet, cell, bit stream, structured bit stream)

today: RFC 3985 is an Informational document that gives the PWE3 architecture, and it is updated by RFC 5462. It leaves encapsulation formats and signaling to other documents.

sections.title: What a Pseudo Wire Is
sections.content:
A pseudo wire (PW) emulates the essential attributes of a telecommunications service, such as a T1 leased line or Frame Relay, over a packet switched network (PSN) that uses IP or MPLS. The RFC supports the requirements in RFC 3916. The goal is only the minimum functionality needed to emulate the wire with the required faithfulness for a given service.

PWs encapsulate service-specific bit streams, cells or PDUs arriving at an ingress port and carry them across an IP path or MPLS tunnel, managing timing and order where needed. To the customer equipment, a PW looks like an unshared link or circuit of the chosen service. Where the emulation is imperfect, the limits must be described in the service-specific documents. The RFC states that the on-the-wire encapsulations and the detailed setup protocols are non-goals.
sections.eli5: A pseudo wire is a pretend cable. The two computers at the ends think they have their own private cable, but really their data rides inside a shared network.

sections.title: Payload Types
sections.content:
The RFC sorts what a PW carries into four generic payload types. A packet payload is a variable-size unit such as an Ethernet frame or an HDLC frame, and may need fragmentation if it is too big for the PSN path. A cell payload is a fixed-size group of octets, such as the 53-octet ATM cell or the 188-octet MPEG Transport Stream packet. Several cells may be put in one payload to cut per-packet overhead.

A bit stream payload is captured and replayed without using its internal structure. A structured bit stream uses knowledge of that structure, for example by stripping SONET section and line overhead and restoring it at the far end.

A guiding rule is minimum intervention: carry the payload as received, with as few changes as possible, following RFC 1958. Any intermediate format becomes a new framing type that needs documenting and interoperability work.
sections.eli5: Different things travel over wires: whole letters, equal-sized postcards, or a never-ending ribbon. The pretend cable needs a slightly different way to pack each kind, but it should change the contents as little as possible.

sections.title: The Reference Model
sections.content:
The network reference model has two provider edge devices (PE1 and PE2) that serve customer edge devices (CE1 and CE2). A CE connects to its PE over an attachment circuit (AC), such as an ATM VPI/VCI, a Frame Relay DLCI, an Ethernet port or a VLAN. Between the PEs, a PSN tunnel carries one or more PWs. Native data units arrive on the AC, are encapsulated in a PW-PDU and cross the tunnel. The PW traffic is invisible to the core, and the core is transparent to the CEs.

The model also allows pre-processing in the PE, made of two parts. A forwarder (FWRD) selects which PW to use for a payload that arrives on an AC. Native service processing (NSP) does work that needs knowledge of the payload, such as translating identifiers. The details of FWRD and NSP are outside PWE3, and the RFC says NSP lets a PW stay simple and homogeneous.
sections.eli5: Two post offices each have a customer at the door. The post offices use a shared highway between them, and the customers never see it. They only see a private mail slot that seems to lead straight to the other customer.

sections.title: Layers and Encapsulation
sections.content:
The logical layering has a payload on top, an optional Encapsulation layer, a PW Demultiplexer layer, an optional PSN Convergence layer, then the PSN itself. The demultiplexer lets many PWs share one tunnel. Its identifier can be an MPLS label, an L2TP session ID or a UDP port number. The Encapsulation layer has three sub-layers: payload convergence, timing and sequencing. Timing and sequencing are optional and omitted when a PW does not need them.

Sequencing gives frame ordering, duplicate detection and loss detection. The RFC notes a sequence number space larger than 2^16 may be needed to avoid wrapping during a network transient. Timing covers clock recovery and timed delivery, and the RFC prefers RTP (RFC 3550) where suitable. Fragmentation should be avoided where possible. A PE does not have to support it, and a PE that does not will drop packets that exceed the PSN MTU.

Over MPLS, an inner label does the demultiplexing, and a four-octet control word carries flags, fragmentation, length and sequence information compactly. For MPLS PSNs, the first four bits of a PW packet must not look like an IP version number in current use.
sections.eli5: A parcel gets wrapped in layers: first its own box, then a label that says which pretend cable it belongs to, then the shipping crate for the highway. Some wrappers are skipped when the parcel does not need them.

sections.title: Control Plane and Management
sections.content:
A PW must be set up before use and torn down afterward. Setup can be triggered by an operator, by signaling of an AC, or by auto-discovery, and manual configuration is allowed. During setup the PEs exchange a PW-TYPE identifier, which is used to check that the attachment circuits are compatible and to mitigate misconnection. The RFC says PWE3 needs a reliable control channel plus one or more data channels, and says the signaling protocol for the PSN tunnel itself is out of scope.

Native services that have failure notification, status monitoring or keep-alive mechanisms need equivalents on the emulated service. A group ID can report the status of many emulated services at once. If best-effort traffic is not known to be TCP friendly, PEs should watch the loss rate and may rate-limit or shut down PWs. For management, the RFC describes layered SNMP MIB modules: a service layer, a generic PW layer and a PSN VC layer. It also says a connection verification mechanism should be supported.
sections.eli5: Before the pretend cable works, both ends agree what kind of cable it is. After that they keep checking it is alive, and if something breaks they tell the people at the other end.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
PWE3 provides no means of protecting the integrity, confidentiality or delivery of the native data units. Assumptions that hold on a point-to-point or circuit-switched network may not hold on an emulated wire. For example, the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol relies on relatively weak security when nodes share a LAN, and that is a bigger weakness on an emulated Ethernet.

The RFC advises controlling access to the PW tunnel endpoint and validating traffic addressed to the PW demultiplexer, to resist spoofing. IPsec may be used between the two PEs, but it cannot protect the native service itself.
sections.eli5: A pretend cable is not a locked pipe. Anyone with access to the shared highway could try to sneak in fake parcels, so the post offices need to check who is sending to them.
